newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 19.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 19.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

MUNICH - Bavaria's Hypo-Bank says it has assigned a "significantly higher" advertising budget to agency TBWA to launch an image study and put together plans for a campaign to be led by TBWA. Four agencies, including Munich-based Wueschner und Rohwer, competed for the contract. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - After snatching pharmaceutical giant Bayer as a client, Duesseldorf's DDB has now won Cologne-based commercial TV channel Super RTL. Rivals in the pitch were BMZ/FCA, Start Advertising and Super RTL's former agency Huth + Wenzel.
(Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BONN - Bernd Kundrun, managing director of pay-TV channel

Premiere, is to switch to publishing group Gruner+Jahr-Verlags (G+J) in August, Bertelsmann-unit G+J says. G+J denies that Kundrun's move from Premiere has anything to do with negotiations between Bertelsmann and the Kirch group over the future of Premiere, in which both have interests. German news magazines have reported that Kirch had demanded the dismissal
of Kundrun. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Increasing numbers of German Internet users are
using the Internet to make purchases and gain information about products and services, according to a survey of 16,000 users.
(Handelsblatt)
BONN - Germany's millions of Turkish residents feel
inadequately informed by the media, according to survey
findings unveiled by the government. The survey however also discovered that around a half only ever read Turkish-language newspapers. (Reuter)

NUREMBERG - A consortium of institutional investors led by industrial holding group DBAG is to take a majority stake in printing and publishing group Sebaldus. Sebaldus says the deal is designed to give it the capital for further expansion and was not intended to include management control. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - Carmaker Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp, launches the largest product offensive in its history, offering 26 new models by the end of 2001. Opel says the new models will include eight new small trucks and that six new vehicles will be offered in 1998 alone, including the new compact van Zafira that will be unveiled in September at the
Frankfurt car show. (Reuter)
STUTTGART - Two of the motoring world's legendary names,

Porsche AG and Harley-Davidson Inc, are teaming up to make motorcycle engine parts. Porsche says each company will contribute $10 million to the project in which the U.S. motorcycle maker would hold the controlling 51 percent stake.
(Reuter)
